Gremlin officials are praising a decision by President Trump
to exempt Russia from a U.S. sanctions bill passed by Congress last month.
The measure had been intended to exert more, not less,
economic pressure on Moscow over its war against Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Zelensky slammed the decision as unfortunate,
and Piers Charles Maynes has more.
With an executive order, Trump exempted Russia
from a punishing congressional sanctions package set to take effect Sunday,
arguing the waiver was in the U.S.'s national interest.
The measure, signed by Trump into law last month,
had sought to impose deep tariffs on Russian energy sales
and tighten sanctions on senior Kremlin officials,
including President Vladimir Putin.
The Kremlin's U.S. envoy, Kirill Dimitriev, called the waiver truly historic,
saying the law threatened global economic growth.
The move comes a week after Trump agreed to purchase sanctioned Russian diesel
in an attempt to tamp down U.S. gas prices ahead of the midterm elections.
Ukraine has condemned the fuel deal, saying it helps Russia fund the war.
Charles Maynes, NPR News, Moscow.
No King's rallies are taking place across the country today.
In the past, the protests have been against President Trump,
but today they have a new focus, voting.
And Piers Ava Berger has more.
Superhero capes and masks.
That's what you'll find at Cammie Dunford's "Voting is Your Superpower" event
today in Frisco, Texas.
I have a T-shirt that says "Voting is My Superpower" and I have the cape.
And, yeah, we're ready.
Dunford and her advocacy group, Indivisible Frisco,
also made 500 mini goodie bags.
In each one are QR codes with resources on voting in Texas.
Dunford's event is one of thousands across the country.
They're all part of the No King's Vote Early initiative.
Unlike past protests, organizers say the goal today
is direct non-partisan action, getting people out to the polls.
Ava Berger, NPR News.
Widespread protests continue in France today,
where student-led protests about school conditions have grown into broader ones
against the policies of French President Emmanuel Macron.
There has been some violence today and protesters are clashing with police
who are using tear gas and water cannons in some places.
And Piers' Eleanor Beersley is among some of those demonstrating in the streets of Paris.
I am out in a protest march in Paris of mostly young people,
and it's peaceful.
And they're marching for their usual conditions
to just study in normal conditions and not dilapidated facilities.
But France is a split screen today because we've also seen horrible violence.
Fires, for example, in the city of Lyon, they burnt down the tourism bureau
and in Marseille, they broke into the ornate town hall
using street bear cases, a battering ram.
And Piers' Eleanor Beersley reporting from Paris.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
The U.S. territory of Guam is bracing for a super typhoon.
Typhoon Champion, currently a strong Category 4 storm,
is expected to pass just south of the island.
Dana Williams from member station KPRG on Guam has more.
Residents of Guam were urged to secure their homes
and evacuate from low-lying coastal areas
as the dangerous typhoon approached the island.
Brandon Eitlett of the National Weather Service on Guam
described the situation as a near-worst-case scenario.
Champion is rapidly intensifying,
and we are looking at a Category 4 150-mph super typhoon
at the time early Sunday morning around closest point of approach.
Residents were warned to take shelter in reinforced concrete buildings
and to remain in place until the all-clear is given.
Forecasters said the island will likely experience widespread power outages,
possibly lasting for days or weeks.
Champy will be the third super typhoon
to hit the Mariana island chain in the western Pacific this year.
For NPR News, I'm Dana Williams on Guam.
Pope Leo is out of the hospital days after lung cancer surgery.
Yesterday he celebrated Mass in the hospital in Rome,
and tomorrow he's scheduled to deliver the traditional noon blessing
from a window that overlooks St. Peter's Square.
The 71-year-old had the right lower lobe of his lung removed,
and test results on whether the cancer has spread aren't in yet.
Leo has a trip to Latin America scheduled for next month,
but the Vatican hasn't commented yet on whether that will still take place.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.
